news.title: The Club World Cup deals the knockout blow to Infantino
news.lede: Aleksander Ceferin, president of European football's governing body (UEFA), and Nasser Al-Khelaifi, chairman of the European Club Association, are holding an anticipated meeting in the city of Salzburg. Tension is rising between their organisations and world football's governing body (FIFA), specifically against its president Gianni Infantino. According to the "talkSPORT" network, the root of that tension lies in the possibility of the European clubs withdrawing from the 2029 Club World Cup, following UEFA's decision regarding the national teams in relation to the World Cup. Spanish newspaper "AS" reported that there is as yet no agreement between the European Club Association and FIFA to stage the 2029 Club World Cup, which makes talk of boycotting the tournament inaccurate for now.

news.title: Gianni Infantino latest: Key questions as Fifa president faces executives
news.lede: Gianni Infantino has been Fifa president since 2016. Fifa president Gianni Infantino will meet with senior leaders of football's world governing body on Wednesday as criticism of his now scrapped plan to sell off Fifa's commercial and event operations intensifies. After secretary general Mattias Grafstrom sent a highly critical internal memo to Fifa staff, Infantino summoned members of the Fifa management board to Morocco. Tuesday also saw chief of global football development Arsene Wenger insist he was "not involved" in Infantino's Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal, adding that aborting it was "absolutely necessary and beyond question".

news.title: Jamie Carragher claims Arsene Wenger asked him to endorse controversial FIFA World Cup idea to fans
news.lede: Jamie Carragher talked about being approached by the legendary Arsenal manager, who has since joined FIFA, to endorse a proposal many fans were against. FIFA as an organisation have come under fire over the last few months, despite the enormous success of the FIFA World Cup this summer. Gianni Infantino’s attempt to privatise the FIFA World Cup through a subsidiary was instantly rejected. But years ago, FIFA tried floating a far more controversial idea, one helmed by one of football’s great managers.

news.title: World Cup thug Paredes given police protection with riot shield during corner
news.lede: LEANDRO PAREDES required protection from a riot cop with a shield during a recent match. The controversial Argentina star, 32, hit the headlines for his World Cup final meltdown last month. Paredes committed several fouls during the match before letting his temper boil over after the final whistle. The midfielder grabbed Eric Garcia before flooring Gavi and was shown a red card.

news.title: Roma strike agreement with Atletico Madrid for World Cup finalist Molina
news.lede: Wednesday’s reports claim that Roma have found an agreement with Atletico Madrid over a transfer fee for 2022 World Cup winner and 2026 runner-up Nahuel Molina. Roma submitted an offer for the 28-year-old Argentine full-back on Tuesday afternoon, and according to the latest updates from transfer specialist Gianluca Di Marzio, Atletico have accepted a proposal worth €13m plus up to €4m in bonuses. The clubs are reportedly working on the final details before Atletico formally sanction the player’s departure. Molina has spent the last four seasons in the Spanish capital with Atletico, having joined in a €15m deal from Udinese in the summer of 2022.

news.lede: Turkiye club Trabzonspor say they have begun negotiations to sign the Egyptian star forward. Fallout from failed FIFA World Cup selloff continues, as Jordan FA president joins list of Gianni Infantino detractors. FIFA refutes report that its President Gianni Infantino sought Donald Trump’s backing after failed World Cup selloff. Five influential African football leaders back Gianni Infantino amid World Cup private investment row.

news.title: Billionaire Patrice Motsepe and CAF executives backs Infantino after FIFA drops plan to "sell the World Cup" for $4.2 billion
news.lede: Patrice Motsepe, the billionaire president of the Confederation of African Football (CAF), has spearheaded a wave of support for FIFA President Gianni Infantino despite a growing rift in global football governance. This surge of loyalty from the continent follows Infantino’s decision to abandon a controversial proposal to raise $4.2 billion by selling minority stakes in a new commercial rights body. While regional bodies in Europe, Asia, and North America have recently declared a loss of confidence in Infantino’s leadership, the 54-member African bloc remains his most vital base of political power heading into the next FIFA presidential election. The controversy centered on a project known as the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a proposed $20 billion subsidiary designed to manage the World Cup and other major events.
